prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1060; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the policyholder's household member, who reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant reported a knee injury and said they were not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. They described the same sequence as the first report: the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they were merging, and their side panels made contact. They gave the same account of the impact without prompting.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. The officer's notes place the claimant outside the vehicle when the collision occurred, which conflicts with the claimant's own statement and needs to be clarified before any injury evaluation is finalized.

Entry 4: Reviewed photos from the scene and the other driver's statement. Both show contact along the right side of the vehicle, consistent with the described impact. A witness statement also describes the collision as the claimant reported it, though the witness did not see who was inside the vehicle.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The damage pattern matches the impact described by the claimant and the other driver. No prior body damage or repairs to the same area were found in the records or on inspection, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: Requested medical records. The knee injury is the kind expected from a force of this type. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the file shows no earlier problems with the same knee.

Entry 7: Confirmed with the policy records that the driver involved lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy. Coverage applies to the driver for this loss, subject to the open question about the claimant's location at the time of the crash.

Entry 8: Followed up with the claimant again to address the officer's and witness's accounts about their position at impact. The claimant repeated their original account, and the file remains open pending the medical review and that clarification.
